## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design an on-device ML feature with privacy, latency, and budget constraints, plus a clear go/no-go decision after a year.

## Key Concepts
- On-device inference and model size
- Latency targets and worst-case tail latency
- Privacy/compliance costs and user consent
- Cloud verification as a fallback vs full-on cloud processing
- Rollout strategy, offline fallback behavior, drift/maintenance, break-even planning

## Code Example
```javascript
function estimateEnergy(inferenceMs, cpuPowerMw, invocationsPerHour) {
  return (inferenceMs * cpuPowerMw * invocationsPerHour) / 1000;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate privacy guarantees while collecting metrics?
- How would you handle model updates without increasing memory footprint significantly?

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to reason holistically about on-device ML trade-offs in an enterprise context, balancing privacy requirements, technical constraints, regulatory compliance, and business economics.

## Key Concepts

- **On-device ML constraints**: Model quantization, memory footprint, and CPU energy consumption
- **Latency requirements**: Differentiating live (real-time) vs. post-call summarization latency targets
- **Local telemetry and storage**: Privacy implications of on-device data handling
- **Multilingual support**: Model management and memory trade-offs across languages
- **Cloud feedback vs. offline updates**: Security and privacy considerations for optional cloud connectivity
- **Regulatory compliance**: GDPR, CCPA, and associated implementation costs
- **Business case development**: Rollout planning, go/no-go criteria, and break-even analysis

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a cost-benefit framework around privacy-preserving client-side data handling, including on-device processing, user consent, and regulatory considerations. It also probes rollout planning and measurable business impact across multiple platforms.

## Key Concepts
- On-device processing (WASM), privacy by design, consent-driven telemetry
- PII redaction, signature of data blobs, minimal data transfer
- Compliance budgeting, audit readiness, regional rollout
- Metrics: CPU, energy, storage, blob size, consent rate, support load impact

## Code Example
```javascript
function redactPII(payload){
  const s = JSON.stringify(payload);
  return s.replace(/"(name|email|phone|address)":"[^"]+"/g, '"$1":"REDACTED"');
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you model break-even sensitivity to consent-rate changes?
- What fallbacks exist if device performance degrades on older hardware?
